title: Enable Vectorscan on Windows arm64 while preserving the current backend matrix
assumptions: The previous backend-matrix task is already implemented and merged.
All current platform defaults except Windows arm64 should remain unchanged.
Windows arm64 is currently the only target being promoted from Qt-only to an accelerated backend in this task.
objective: Change Windows arm64 from Qt-only to Vectorscan, using ZEACENT/klogg as a practical MSVC/Vectorscan reference, while preserving the rest of the current matrix and keeping regex matching performance as the top priority.
priority_order: Regex matching performance on Windows arm64
Correct and explicit Windows arm64 Vectorscan enablement
Runtime correctness and Qt fallback behavior
Maintainability and clarity of backend selection

windows-arm64.notes: Use the fastest supported non-fat Windows arm64 configuration. Do not keep this target on Qt by default anymore.

purpose: Reference for Vectorscan integration on Windows with MSVC
Reference for CI/workflow structure for Windows plus Vectorscan builds
Reference for dependency wiring, compile definitions, logging, and packaging labels where applicable
rules: Use ZEACENT/klogg as an implementation reference, not as a source of truth for this repo's architecture matrix.
Copy ideas only where they fit the current dm17ryk/klogg codebase cleanly.
Do not blindly copy unrelated platform choices from ZEACENT/klogg.

hard_constraints: Do not change the default backend for Windows x64, Linux x64, Linux arm64, macOS x64, or macOS arm64.
Do not revert Windows arm64 to Qt-only by default.
Do not introduce runtime fallback from Vectorscan to Hyperscan or from Hyperscan to Vectorscan. Backend choice remains build-time.
Qt regex remains the only runtime fallback when backend validation or initialization fails.
Do not enable Linux-only fat-runtime assumptions on Windows arm64.
Prefer a native Windows arm64 Vectorscan path over SIMDe or other emulation-style fallbacks.
Do not make SIMDe the default backend path for Windows arm64. If a SIMDe-based escape hatch is added at all, it must be explicit, isolated, documented, and non-default.
Preserve manual override flags where practical, but unsupported combinations must fail clearly at configure time.
If both accelerated backends are enabled simultaneously, fail configuration with a clear error.

tasks: Update backend auto-selection so Windows arm64 defaults to Vectorscan.
Preserve the already-implemented defaults for all other platform and architecture combinations.
Normalize architecture detection across CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR, KLOGG_ARCH, MSVC generator platform, and any existing repo-specific helpers.
Recognize at minimum: x86_64, AMD64, x64, arm64, aarch64, ARM64.
Emit a configure-time summary that clearly reports target OS, target architecture, selected backend, and whether fat runtime is enabled.

implementation_requirements.area: Third-party dependency wiring for Windows arm64
tasks: Make sure Windows arm64 selects the Vectorscan dependency path in 3rdparty/CMakeLists.txt.
Audit all Vectorscan CMake options for Windows arm64 and remove any x86-only or Linux-only assumptions from this target.
Keep Windows arm64 on a performance-oriented non-fat configuration by default.
Keep USE_CPU_NATIVE off by default for distributable Windows arm64 builds unless there is a very strong repo-specific reason to do otherwise.
If additional ARM64-specific generator, toolset, or compiler conditionals are needed for MSVC, add them explicitly and document them.
Use ZEACENT/klogg as a reference for getting Vectorscan to compile with MSVC, but adapt the solution to this repo's current structure.
Ensure runtime code can explicitly distinguish Hyperscan vs Vectorscan.
If the repo currently uses backend-specific compile definitions from the previous task, preserve and extend them cleanly for Windows arm64.
Do not rely on a generic accelerated-backend macro if backend-specific behavior now differs materially.
Make sure Windows arm64 Vectorscan activation does not depend on x86-only SSE2 or SSSE3 gates.
Prefer backend-native validation such as hs_valid_platform() plus actual database and scratch initialization outcomes.
If Vectorscan validation or initialization fails at runtime, fall back to Qt regex with a clear log message that includes backend name, target architecture, and failure reason.
Keep the runtime path cleanly shared with the already-working Linux arm64 and macOS arm64 Vectorscan logic where possible.

implementation_requirements.area: CPU feature detection and compiler flags
tasks: Audit src/utils/src/cpu_info.cpp so Windows arm64 no longer looks unsupported merely because x86 CPUID logic is absent.
Keep CPU feature detection for diagnostics or optional optimizations only; it must not be the deciding gate that disables Vectorscan on Windows arm64.
Ensure x86-only compiler flags such as AVX2 or x86-only intrinsics are never applied on Windows arm64.
If needed, add Windows arm64-specific diagnostic reporting, but do not block backend activation on missing x86 probes.

implementation_requirements.area: Windows arm64 CI and build verification
tasks: Update .github/workflows/ci-build.yml so Windows arm64 builds with Vectorscan enabled by default.
Use an MSVC ARM64 configuration explicitly, for example a Visual Studio generator with platform ARM64 or an equivalent supported approach.
Make backend choice visible in job names, configure output, artifact names, or package labels.
If the CI environment can only cross-compile but not execute Windows arm64 binaries, compile verification is acceptable in CI, but add a short manual verification note for real hardware or emulation.
Update BUILD.md and any relevant README or build docs to state that Windows arm64 now uses Vectorscan by default.
Document that Windows arm64 uses a non-fat Vectorscan configuration in this step.
Document any special MSVC or generator requirements for Windows arm64 builds.
Document any explicit remaining limitations, such as runtime verification being compile-only in CI if execution is unavailable.
Keep the Windows arm64 Vectorscan path organized so future Windows-specific tuning can be added without reworking backend selection again.
Do not entangle Windows arm64 logic with Linux-only fat-runtime or ELF-specific assumptions.

manual_override_rules: Keep manual overrides for developers where practical.
If KLOGG_USE_VECTORSCAN=ON on Windows arm64, this is now a supported path and must build or fail clearly with a reproducible reason.
If KLOGG_USE_HYPERSCAN=ON on Windows arm64, fail configure clearly unless there is already an explicitly supported path in the repo.
If both KLOGG_USE_HYPERSCAN=OFF and KLOGG_USE_VECTORSCAN=OFF, Qt-only mode remains a valid explicit override.
acceptance_criteria: Auto-selection chooses Vectorscan on Windows arm64.
Auto-selection for all other targets remains unchanged from the previous matrix task.
Windows arm64 configure output clearly reports Vectorscan as the selected backend.
Windows arm64 Vectorscan no longer depends on x86-only SSE2 or SSSE3 checks to activate.
Windows arm64 no longer defaults to Qt-only.
Qt fallback still works when Vectorscan validation, database compilation, or scratch allocation fails at runtime.
Windows arm64 CI is updated to build with Vectorscan enabled.
Windows arm64 uses a non-fat configuration by default.
No x86-only compiler flags leak into the Windows arm64 build.
The implementation remains compatible with the existing accelerated backend flow on the other supported targets.

configure_checks: Configure Windows arm64 with default settings and confirm Vectorscan is selected.
Configure Windows x64, Linux x64, Linux arm64, macOS x64, and macOS arm64 and confirm their existing defaults are unchanged.
Verify the configure summary prints OS, architecture, backend, and fat-runtime mode.
build_checks: Build Windows arm64 in Release or RelWithDebInfo with MSVC and confirm Vectorscan compiles and links.
Confirm Windows arm64 does not pull in x86-only AVX2 or SSE-only compilation paths.
Confirm the CI workflow reflects the new Windows arm64 backend selection.
runtime_checks: Where execution is possible, run a minimal regex smoke test on Windows arm64 and confirm Vectorscan path activation or clear Qt fallback logging.
If CI cannot execute Windows arm64 binaries, provide a small manual verification recipe for local ARM64 hardware or emulation.
regression_checks: Verify no target links both Hyperscan and Vectorscan simultaneously.
Verify Linux arm64 and macOS arm64 Vectorscan paths remain intact.
Verify Windows x64 remains Hyperscan by default.

non_goals: Do not switch Windows x64, Linux x64, or macOS x64 away from Hyperscan.
Do not reopen the broader backend-matrix design unless required for a narrowly scoped fix.
Do not reintroduce Windows arm64 as Qt-only by default.
Do not enable Linux-style fat runtime on Windows arm64.
Do not make SIMDe or another emulation-oriented path the default unless native Windows arm64 Vectorscan is provably impossible and the tradeoff is explicitly documented.
deliverables: Code changes enabling Vectorscan by default on Windows arm64.
Updated CI/workflow configuration for Windows arm64 plus Vectorscan.
Updated documentation describing the Windows arm64 backend.
A concise PR summary explaining how Windows arm64 Vectorscan was wired, what was borrowed conceptually from ZEACENT/klogg, and any remaining upstream or toolchain caveats.
suggested_pr_title: Enable Vectorscan on Windows arm64 and preserve the current platform backend matrix
final_response_requirements: List exactly which files were changed.
State the final backend matrix after this task.
Explicitly confirm that Windows arm64 now uses Vectorscan by default.
State that Windows arm64 is non-fat in this step.
Call out any remaining MSVC, upstream, or runtime limitations.
Describe whether the Windows arm64 CI step is compile-only or includes runtime verification.
prompt_for_codex: Implement this task exactly as specified. Assume the previous matrix task is already merged. Change only Windows arm64 from Qt-only to Vectorscan, while preserving all other platform defaults. Use ZEACENT/klogg as a practical reference for getting Vectorscan to compile with MSVC, but do not blindly copy its full platform strategy. Keep Windows arm64 on the fastest supported non-fat Vectorscan configuration. Do not require x86-only SSE2 or SSSE3 checks on Windows arm64. Prefer backend-native validation such as hs_valid_platform() and actual initialization outcomes. Keep Qt as the only runtime fallback. Update CI and documentation accordingly.
